title: Base change of the inverse-integration normal factor
statement: Fix a finite purity setting P [def-pur-conventions] and a normalized etale compact-support datum N. Let aB:B->Spec k and aBprime:Bprime->Spec k be separated finite-type structure maps, b:Bprime->B any morphism with aB b=aBprime, and X=(g:V->B,s), Xprime=(gprime:Vprime->Bprime,sprime) smooth separated quasi-compact pure-dimension-d pairs with closed sections. Fix their Cartesian base-change datum sq [def-pur-section-restriction-data]. Write normalBaseChange(sq) for its canonical pulled-back normal pair and c_N for the counit-defined section exchange along it. Then normalIntegration(Xprime) c_N = Tate_b b^*(normalIntegration(X)), where normalIntegration is the actual conormal-model construction of [def-pur-normal-section-integration-data], and Tate_b is the specified pro-etale Tate pullback [def-pur-section-tate-pullback]. This statement involves only the normal pairs, not the DNC-specialization maps delta. No flatness or positive-rank assumption is made; empty bases are included.

source.place: Proof (1), normal-bundle base change and inverse vector-integration square

proof.text: Base change of the homogeneous Rees algebra fixes the deformation coordinate and pulls back homogeneous ideal classes. At zero the symmetric conormal comparison therefore intertwines the actual normal-base-change map with pullback of the conormal bundle, preserving projection and zero.

For the integration adjunct gamma, integration-normalized vector-bundle purity gives E b^*(gamma)=gamma_prime T, with E the exceptional exchange and T Tate pullback. Multiplication by inverse adjuncts gives gamma_prime inverse E=T b^*(gamma inverse). Restrict along the zero section; the zero-section equation and pullback compositor give the ordinary-etale normal-section square.

The normalized etale-locality factor in normalIntegration and the counit-defined pro-etale exchange agree after site comparison. Indeed both are mates of inverse compact-support exchange followed by the pulled-back counit. Use vector-integration site comparison and finite-level compact-support comparison, then mate pasting, to identify them. Naturality of comparison pullback and Tate maps yields the stated square. The rank-zero trace is the identity; for empty bases all these same maps are unique.

theorem normalIntegration_baseChange (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (N : Etale.EtaleCompactSupportNormalization P.Coefficient)
    {B' B : Scheme.{u}} {d : ℕ}
    (aB : B ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [IsSeparated aB]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aB] [QuasiCompact aB]
    (aB' : B' ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [IsSeparated aB']
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aB'] [QuasiCompact aB']
    (b : B' ⟶ B) (_hb : b ≫ aB = aB')
    (X : Pair B d) (X' : Pair B' d) (sq : BaseChange b X' X) :
    baseComparison P aB aB' (normalBaseChange P aB aB' sq) ≪≫
        normalIntegration P N aB' X' =
      (ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient) b).leftDerivedFunctor.mapIso
          (normalIntegration P N aB X) ≪≫ OrientationRefinement.tate P b aB d
